generator_metadata.summary: A zero-background grid contains 3..6 same-color four-connected objects. Replace every odd-sized object by color 3 and every even-sized object by color 8, preserving all occupied coordinates.

review_brief:
# Review — 2243318b8e96 / generator 3.0.0

Defect → repair: the imported base lacked `RULE_HASH`, had dead/degenerate axes,
permissive scalar handling, and weak canonical coverage. I replaced it with a
strict constructive sampler over four observable axes while preserving the exact
canonical odd→3/even→8 Racket rule.

The native `parity_reference` family adds `same_as_cue` and `opposite_to_cue` to
the exact `absolute` default. A unique color-1 object's size parity is the
input-derived intermediate consumed by the alternative rules. Two crossed demos
identify all three settings; four distinct queries include a distributed 30×30
stress scene.

Actual adversarial findings repaired: diagonal-anchor drift under shape flips,
a component-identity error in the mutation probe, a surviving total-foreground
parity shortcut, and an overbroad canonical-shortcut declaration. Final checks
include 22/22 focused tests, 120/120 Racket/mirror base applications, 22,230/22,230
override draws, 12/12 identifiable base lessons, 96 parametric episodes with 960
shortcut attacks, six source-bound preflight jobs / 60 protected-Racket runs, a
replayed wrong-intermediate causal witness, and 24 verified one-query views.

One aggregate battery invocation was interrupted by the foreground controller after lint/self-check; every cited stage was rerun independently against the same final source.

Finite checks are not a proof over every grid or heuristic. The artifact is
reviewer-ready only; owner acceptance and training admission remain pending.

previous_catalog_record.summary: 0-bg grid (h ∈ 8-12, w ∈ 8-12) with: N_BLOBS ∈ 3-5 NON-TOUCHING BLOBS, each in a DISTINCT non-bg color drawn from {1..9}, each with a DISTINCT SIZE drawn from {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} (so all sizes differ). At least one ODD and at least one EVEN size are forced (sizes[0] swapped to 3 if all even, or to 4 if all odd) so the parity rule has visible contrast. Each blob built by _grow_blob with 1-cell padding from existing blobs (via _has_neighbor check). Rule (RECOLOR EACH BLOB'S CELLS BY ITS SIZE'S PARITY: ODD SIZE → COLOR 3, EVEN SIZE → COLOR 8): EXTRACT every 4-connected non-bg COMPONENT. For EACH blob: COMPUTE cell count k. IF k IS ODD: PAINT every cell of the blob with COLOR 3 (green). IF k IS EVEN: PAINT with COLOR 8 (cyan). Original colors are overwritten; positions preserved. Net: blob sizes encoded as parity; odd → green, even → cyan, no other colors survive.

scope: Accepted generator repair; finite reviewer evidence, no new maintainer execution

parametric_work.limits: Finite reviewer/adversarial support only; universal uniqueness is not proved. The preflight is authoring evidence, not owner native qualification/acceptance. Training admission remains pending.

sequential_dependency.intermediate: One input-derived cue-parity bit: cue_size mod 2, with 0 for even and 1 for odd.
sequential_dependency.step_a: Locate the unique color-1 4-connected component and compute its cell-count parity.
sequential_dependency.step_b: For every foreground component, compare its cell-count parity with the cue bit; under same_as_cue paint equal parity 3 and unequal parity 8.
sequential_dependency.why_b_depends_on_a: The correct output class is equality to the input-derived cue parity. Before A produces that bit, B cannot know whether odd or even components belong to color 3; substituting the wrong bit changes the final grid.

parametric_work.summary: Native adapter supports parity_reference=absolute|same_as_cue|opposite_to_cue, 2–6 demonstrations, exactly four distinct matched-input queries, protected-Racket labels, a substantive 30×30 stress query, and a replayed A→cue-parity→component-recoloring witness.

target_report.summary: Repaired the canonical size-parity sampler and strict call contract; built a source-bound parity_reference family with an exact canonical default, two cue-relative alternatives, crossed minimum lessons, four queries including 30x30, a protected-Racket causal witness, and bounded shortcut/export attacks.
